object_description: central building with an attached high-rise landmark
design_condition: The campus is distributed across an existing industrial ensemble, a new central building and a high-rise, with the high-rise extending the central building toward the city and student housing completing the campus perimeter.

positive.statement: The project is characterized by an in-depth analysis of the prevailing context.

position.rationale: The compact central block and attached vertical volume visibly form a context-responsive ensemble.

positive.statement: The high-rise serves as a landmark and is adequately integrated into the urban development situation.

position.rationale: The tall attached mass is clearly distinguished from the lower central building across the elevations.

positive.statement: The head building is a strong identity-creating element and interactive interface between the public and the university.

position.rationale: The lower central block is visibly separate from the attached high-rise and anchors the ensemble.

positive.statement: The factory halls become a very communicative think tank.

position.rationale: The lower horizontal volume provides the closest sampled anchor for the factory-hall zone.

positive.statement: The proposed operating concept is plausible and has many good ideas.

position.rationale: The central building footprint is used as a broad constrained anchor for the operational concept.

positive.statement: The architectural expression is strong and corresponds to a technical, innovative institution.

position.rationale: The east-facing elevation clearly shows the strong technical expression of the multi-volume ensemble.

negative.statement: Simply accommodating the identity-creating uses in the high-rise is viewed as critical because it does not promote lively exchange.

position.rationale: The upper portion of the distinct high-rise is clearly visible as the criticized identity-use location.
